done_state: tessera/store/ provides the SQLite event-sourced storage engine specified in ARCHITECTURE.md: schema + hash chain + transaction discipline + workflow/hierarchy/cycle enforcement + rebuild/verify + backup, proven collision-free under real multi-process concurrency at SCOPE.md's 20x50 bar with realistic in-transaction work. Comments also carry an optional code_snippet field (C25-C30): backward-compatible event payload extension plus a genuine-event backfill path for historical comments, never a projection-only mutation.

criteria.statement: Schema creates an append-only events table: UPDATE and DELETE on events both raise via BEFORE triggers.
events.prev_hash is TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE; the first event uses a fixed non-NULL GENESIS sentinel; a second row cannot reuse it or any other prev_hash.
A BEFORE INSERT trigger rejects an event whose prev_hash is neither the GENESIS sentinel nor an existing event_hash (orphan chain link).

store._write_txn() issues BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and always ROLLBACKs in a finally block (guarded by conn.in_transaction) unless the body reached COMMIT -- a rejected write never leaves the transaction open.
store._write_txn() is not re-entrant: a nested call raises, and the outer transaction still rolls back cleanly (no lock leak).

Ticket creation assigns TESS-N ids atomically and collision-free under >=20 concurrent OS processes x >=50 creates each (>=1000 total), with realistic in-transaction work (workflow+hierarchy+cycle checks actually executing, not a no-op), using the 15-attempt/5000ms retry policy: zero duplicate ids, zero lost writes.
criteria.verification: python3 tests/test_concurrency.py --processes 20 --per-process 50 exits 0 and reports duplicate_ids=0 lost_writes=0.

criteria.statement: A writer process killed with SIGKILL mid-transaction leaves the database recoverable by the next process with no manual intervention: PRAGMA integrity_check reports ok, and no lock remains wedged.
criteria.verification: python3 tests/test_kill_recovery.py exits 0 and reports integrity_check=ok wedged_lock=false.

criteria.statement: Idempotent create: N racing callers using the same idempotency_key produce exactly one ticket and the ticket-id counter advances by exactly one (not N) -- the conflict path rolls back rather than commits.

The idempotency-conflict catch site discriminates the SQLite constraint that fired: it swallows only the idempotency_key conflict and re-raises a prev_hash UNIQUE violation or an orphan-trigger rejection rather than treating either as a duplicate create.
An illegal workflow-status transition is rejected inside store's write transaction (not merely by a caller-side convention) and rolled back.
A Sub-task created without a parent Story/Task/Bug is rejected by store (hierarchy enforced at the store layer).

A blocks/blocked-by link that would create a cycle is rejected by store inside the write transaction, including under concurrent link creation from two processes each adding one edge of the same cycle.

rebuild_projection() replays events from scratch and produces a projection (tickets, ticket_fields, comments, ticket_links, stage_heads) equal to the live projection after a representative sequence of creates/updates/comments/links/archival/stage-promotion events.
verify_chain() reports exactly one root, exactly one tip, zero orphans, and every event_hash matches a fresh recomputation, over a chain built by the normal write path.
Each thread of a multi-threaded process gets its own SQLite connection (threading.local), and every connection sets journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout, and foreign_keys=ON.

Base ticket fields (type, status, reporter, assignee, priority, parent_id, links) and Bug-only fields (severity, repro_steps, environment) are first-class columns/queryable fields, not generic custom fields.
Custom fields (arbitrary key/value beyond the base+Bug set) can be set and read per ticket.
Setting reference_docs on a ticket writes a distinct, visible event (not folded silently into a generic field-update event) recording that the field was used.
project_metadata (codename, prefix) is general, not hardcoded to TESSERA/TESS: a second store instance initialized with a different codename/prefix assigns ids using that prefix with no code change.

Archival (TicketArchived/TicketUnarchived) is an event, not a projection-only mutation: a rebuild_projection() after an archival event reproduces the archived state, and a projection-only mutation (simulated by bypassing store to write the projection directly) is detectable as drift by the rebuild-equality check.
backup() uses VACUUM INTO and produces a valid, consistent snapshot file while concurrent writers are active against the live database.
stage_heads is written only via StagePromoted/StageRolledBack events (never a bare projection write), and is included in rebuild_projection()'s scope.
store refuses to initialize with a clear, loud error if the host's SQLite version is below 3.35 (the UPDATE...RETURNING floor), rather than failing later with an obscure syntax error.

Attachment writes follow temp-write+fsync+rename-to-sha256-path ordering, then the referencing row insert in the same transaction as any other write; a transaction rollback after the rename leaves a collectable orphan blob, never a row pointing at a missing blob.
comments table has a nullable code_snippet TEXT column (schema.py DDL).
add_comment() accepts an optional code_snippet param; when given, it is written into the CommentAdded event payload AND the comments projection row in the same write transaction.

add_comment() with no code_snippet argument (the default) produces a CommentAdded event whose payload has no code_snippet key, and the projection row's code_snippet is NULL -- no behavior change for any existing caller.

rebuild_projection()'s CommentAdded replay handler reads payload.get('code_snippet') (defaulting to None); replaying all pre-existing CommentAdded events (none of which carry the key) reproduces NULL, and rebuild-equals-live still holds across the comments table including the new column.

A new store method, set_comment_code_snippet(ticket_id, comment_id, actor, code_snippet), backfills a historical comment's code_snippet by appending a genuine new CommentCodeSnippetSet event -- never by mutating the existing CommentAdded event or writing the projection directly, per the existing summary/description backfill precedent.
verify_chain() still reports exactly one root, one tip, zero orphans after a backfill sequence of set_comment_code_snippet() calls -- the hash chain is unaffected by the new event type.

failure_criteria.statement: A guard (workflow/hierarchy/cycle/idempotency check) fails open on the path that matters.
failure_criteria.detection: Every guard (C8-C12) has both a rejects-the-bad-case test and a normal-case-still-works test.

failure_criteria.statement: A concurrency/performance number appears in code comments with no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: Every numeric claim in store's source comments must name the exact command that produced it, matching ARCHITECTURE.md's own discipline.

failure_criteria.statement: Code assumes a path, fixture, or the events/counters/project_metadata rows exist without checking.
failure_criteria.detection: store initializes its own schema (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) rather than assuming a pre-existing file.

failure_criteria.statement: An error inside a write transaction is written to a channel nobody reads (e.g. logged and swallowed instead of raised).
failure_criteria.detection: No store method catches a constraint violation or SQLite error and only logs it; every error path either raises to the caller or is an explicitly-modeled idempotency/staleness outcome.

failure_criteria.statement: The 20x50 concurrency evidence run (C6) uses a trivial no-op create instead of exercising the real workflow/hierarchy/cycle checks, making the proof verify nothing (the exact trap ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md's pass-4 F3 finding named).
failure_criteria.detection: test_concurrency.py's harness ticket-create path goes through the same store.create_ticket() used by api, not a stripped-down stand-in.

out_of_scope: git operations themselves (tessera/gitops/) -- store only exposes stage_heads read/write via events; gitops decides when to call it.
Attachment size limits / retention policy (deferred in ARCHITECTURE.md).
Custom-field validation depth beyond typed-and-stored (deferred in ARCHITECTURE.md).
constraints: Python 3.9+ stdlib only (sqlite3, hashlib via tessera.common, threading, subprocess for git-adjacent path checks only).
SQLite >=3.35 (UPDATE...RETURNING) -- checked at startup, host confirmed at 3.51.0/3.53.4.
Every write transaction uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE, isolation_level=None -- never Python's implicit/deferred default.

Retry bound fixed at 15 attempts against busy_timeout=5000ms per ARCHITECTURE.md's measured tuning-trap finding -- do not shorten busy_timeout to retry faster without re-measuring against the full 20x50 bar.
